_comment: Roadmap source of truth. `scripts/sync-roadmap.sh` turns this file into GitHub milestones, labels and issues, and the roadmap-sync workflow replays it on every push to main. The sync is idempotent and additive: it creates what is missing and re-aligns milestone and labels, it never closes an issue and never rewrites a body somebody edited by hand. Each issue is matched by its `key`, not by its title, so a title can be reworded here without opening a duplicate.

labels.name: area:tests
labels.description: unit, CLI, GUI and e2e suites

labels.name: safety
labels.description: touches a safety gate — review with care

milestones.title: v1.1.0
milestones.description: Modular generator and a test suite that generates no load. Split k6/live-event.js into k6/lib, cover the mix, cache classification and summary logic with unit tests, cover the safety gates with CLI tests, and run all of it in CI.

milestones.title: v1.2.0
milestones.description: A browser front-end for the driver: browse profiles, launch a run, watch it, read the history. The GUI is a client of bin/crowdsim — it must not acquire a second, weaker copy of the safety gates.

milestones.title: Backlog
milestones.description: Accepted but unscheduled. Nothing here blocks a release.

issues.title: Tag the 1.0.0 release commit
body: The repository has no tags. `CHANGELOG.md` documents a 1.0.0 release, but the commit that shipped it was never tagged, so `git describe`, the GitHub release list and any consumer pinning a version all see an unreleased repository.
**Done when**
- An annotated tag `v1.0.0` points at the initial release commit.
- Every later release keeps the one-commit-one-tag rule the project already follows.

issues.title: tests/e2e/run.sh: the one suite allowed to generate load
body: `make test-e2e` is documented as the only suite that starts a real generator, and only against a container on the loopback address. The target exists; `tests/e2e/run.sh` does not, so the target fails.
The value of this suite is that it is the only place where a real k6 process, a real profile and a real HTTP origin meet — it is what catches an argument the wrapper composes but k6 rejects.
**Done when**
- `tests/e2e/run.sh` brings up the `cache-ab/` origin, runs a short `load` against it, and asserts on the resulting `out/summary-<run>.json`.
- The run is discarded, loudly, when `generator_ok` is false: a generator-bound run proves nothing.
- The script refuses to start if the target is not a loopback address, so the suite can never be pointed at somebody's infrastructure by editing one variable.
- It skips with a clear message, rather than failing, when docker or k6 is missing.

issues.title: CI: run make lint and make test on push and pull request
body: The unit, CLI and GUI suites run entirely against fakes — a stub k6 on PATH, a temporary profile, a loopback HTTP server — which is exactly what makes them safe to run on a shared CI runner. Nothing runs them today.
**Done when**
- A workflow runs `make lint` and `make test` on push to main and on pull requests.
- `make test-e2e` is **not** part of it: it generates load and needs docker plus k6.
- The job fails on a `bash -n` or `node --check` error, so a syntax break in the driver cannot land.

issues.title: Align the bats invocation between Makefile and package.json
body: `make test-cli` runs `npx bats tests/cli` while `npm run test:cli` runs `bats tests/cli`. The second only works if bats is also installed globally, so the two entry points disagree on a machine that has only the devDependency.
**Done when**
- Both entry points resolve bats the same way, and a clean clone passes after `npm install` alone.

issues.title: README: document the test layout and which suite generates load
body: The split between suites is a safety property, not a convention: `make test` must stay runnable on any machine at any time because it touches nothing outside the checkout, and `make test-e2e` must stay separate because it does not.
**Done when**
- README explains the four suites, what each covers, and states plainly that only the e2e suite generates traffic.
- The `bin/crowdsim` usage header and `AGENTS.md` agree with it.

issues.title: gui/server: profile browsing API
body: `package.json` declares the `gui/server` workspace and `make gui` serves it, but the directory is empty.
First slice: read-only. List the profiles the server is allowed to see, return one for inspection, and report whether it parses and carries an allowlist.
**Done when**
- The server resolves profiles under one configured root and rejects any path that escapes it — a profile path is user input and a profile is a map of somebody's infrastructure.
- A profile with no `safety.allow_hosts` is reported as such rather than silently listed as usable.
- The server binds the loopback interface by default.
- Profile contents are never logged.

issues.title: gui/server: launch a run without weakening the safety gates
body: The GUI must launch runs by invoking `bin/crowdsim`, not by re-implementing argument composition. The driver is where the two gates live, and a second code path that builds k6 arguments is a second place for them to be wrong.
**Done when**
- A run is started as a child process of `bin/crowdsim`; the GUI never calls k6 directly.
- The allowlist gate keeps working end to end: a target outside it fails the run with the driver's own exit code 3, surfaced to the browser.
- `--i-know-this-breaks-production` is never sent by the server. It stays a command-line decision by a human, which is the whole point of it not being a config key.
- The driver's exit codes are propagated verbatim: a tripped brake is an outcome (0), not an error.

issues.title: gui/server: follow a running load test
body: Reading a run means watching it: the knee is visible while it happens, and a summary read afterwards tells you the run tripped the brake without telling you where.
**Done when**
- The server streams the run log to the browser as it is written.
- When the run ends, the summary is delivered and `generator_ok` is displayed prominently — a false value invalidates the run and the UI must say so, not bury it.
- Closing the browser does not kill the run, and reopening it reattaches.

issues.title: gui/ui: run form and history view
body: The `gui/ui` workspace is declared and `make gui-dev` / `make gui-build` target it, but it does not exist.
**Done when**
- A form picks a profile, a target and a shape, and shows the resolved command before it runs — no hidden defaults.
- The history view reads `out/history.tsv` and marks runs with `generator_ok: false` as unusable rather than plotting them next to valid ones.
- The UI states that two runs are only comparable when they used the same URL pool.

issues.title: tests/gui: API tests for profiles, run launching and gate propagation
body: `make test-gui` and `npm run test:gui` both point at `tests/gui/`, which does not exist yet.
**Done when**
- Path traversal against the profile endpoints is covered by a test, not by a code review.
- A test asserts that a target outside the allowlist is refused, and that the server never adds the safe-peak override.
- The suite runs against a stub `crowdsim` on PATH and a loopback server, so it generates no load and needs no k6.

issues.title: Document the GUI: what it is, what it deliberately cannot do
body: **Done when**
- README covers `make gui`, `make gui-dev` and `make gui-build`, and states that the server binds the loopback interface and ships no authentication — it is a local console, not a shared dashboard.
- It says explicitly that the safe-peak override is not available from the GUI, and why.

issues.title: crowdsim validate <profile>: fail on a broken profile before the run
body: A profile that names a journey that does not exist, or a pool file that is missing, currently dies inside the k6 init context with a stack trace — after the operator has already decided to generate load.
**Done when**
- `crowdsim validate <profile>` checks structure, pools, referenced files, class shares and the presence of an allowlist, and reports every problem at once rather than the first.
- It exits 2 on a malformed profile and generates no traffic.
- `doctor` and `load` reuse the same checks, so validation cannot drift from what the run actually requires.

issues.title: crowdsim compare <run-a> <run-b>: a delta between two runs
body: The tool measures deltas honestly and absolutes optimistically, so comparison is the operation that carries meaning. Today it is done by reading two summary files side by side.
**Done when**
- `crowdsim compare` prints per-class latency, error and cache deltas between two runs from `out/`.
- It refuses to compare, rather than quietly comparing, when the two runs used different URL pools or when either has `generator_ok: false`.

issues.title: cache-ab: make the third leg a first-class option
body: `cache-ab/README.md` explains that the useful third leg is the narrow subset of a fix that can actually ship this week, measured in the same run — but adding it means hand-copying a compose service block and a template.
**Done when**
- A third leg can be added without editing the compose file by hand.
- The warning on `candidate.conf.template` about ignoring the origin's `Cache-Control` is carried onto any new template, unchanged.

issues.title: CI: build the container image and smoke-test it
body: The image pins `grafana/k6` and resets its entrypoint so crowdsim drives k6. Nothing checks that the image still builds and still starts after a change to the driver or to the `k6/` layout.
**Done when**
- CI builds the image and runs `crowdsim --help` and `crowdsim doctor` inside it.
- The smoke test asserts that the image refuses to run without an allowlist — the absent default is a feature, and a regression there is the one that matters most.
- No load is generated: the image is never pointed at a network target in CI.
